summary: Add `auth login --chrome/--browser/--profile/--cookies-file` for browser-session cookie auth, alongside the existing bearer-token `auth set-token` path.
reason: Bonusly's confirmed REST API is bearer-token auth via Settings -> API Keys, but not every account can self-serve that token. Ported the Chrome-cookie-extraction pattern from the sibling forkable-pp-cli (pycookiecheat-based: Chrome profile discovery across release channels, cookie-DB inspection, --cookies-file escape hatch) so those accounts can authenticate via a captured browser session instead. New `CookieVal` credential field is fully independent of the existing `AccessToken`/`BonuslyApiToken` bearer path -- AuthHeader() is untouched, so token-based auth has zero regression risk. A new net/http.CookieJar-seeding hook in internal/client (bonusly_cookiejar.go) attaches the captured session to every request via Go's stdlib cookie handling rather than a hand-set Cookie header.
validated_outcome: Live-tested against the real API after a one-time interactive macOS Keychain approval for `auth login --chrome`: `users me --json` and `recognition received --receiver-email ... --json` both returned `meta.source: "live"` with correct data, including receiver_email matching against multi-receiver group bonuses.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generic cookie-session auth support in the generator/machine for CLIs whose auth_type is bearer_token but whose target account cannot self-serve a token
deferred_to_upstream.reason: This patch hand-ports forkable-pp-cli's cookie-extraction machinery per-CLI rather than the generator emitting it from a shared template; the two implementations will drift if either is amended independently.
